Definition: from G3463; a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite number:--ten thousand.
BiblicalUsage: Myrias is a myriad, ten thousand — an innumerable multitude of people gathers to hear Jesus, the church comes to Mount Sion and to an innumerable company of angels, and John hears the voice of many angels round about the throne, ten thousand times ten thousand.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the myriads are the measure of heaven's crowd: uncountable, and every one of them looking at the same throne.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
